[[Group 559]], charged with transporting supplies down the [[Ho Chi Minh Trail]] to supply PAVN troops in both South Vietnam and Laos, numbered 24,400 personnel.{{Cite book|author=Military History Institute of Vietnam |title=Victory in Vietnam: A History of the People's Army of Vietnam, 1954–1975|others=trans. Pribbenow, Merle|publisher=University of Kansas Press|year=2002|isbn=0-7006-1175-4}}{{rp|164–71}} The U.S. estimated the number of [[Viet Cong]] (VC) and PAVN soldiers in South Vietnam at nearly 280,000 by June 1966, including part-time guerrillas.{{cite book|last=Adams|first=Sam |title=War of Numbers: An Intelligence Memoir|publisher=Steerforth Press|year=1994|isbn=1-883642-23-X}}{{rp|63}} A pause in the bombing of North Vietnam by U.S. warplanes had been announced by President Johnson on 24 December and remained in effect. ==January== Writing in ''[[Harper's Magazine]]'' retired U.S. general [[James M. Gavin]] proposed an enclave strategy where U.S. forces would defend coastal enclaves where most of the population and economic activity was concentrated and act as a strategic reserve, leaving the ARVN to fight the PAVN/VC further inland. This strategy was designed not to achieve victory, but rather to create a stalemate forcing the PAVN/VC to seek a negotiated solution. In later years the "Gavin Plan" would become known as "light at the top, heavy at the bottom" reflecting the population concentration of South Vietnam.{{cite book|last=Haycraft|first=William|title=Unraveling Vietnam: How American Arms and Diplomacy Failed in Southeast Asia|publisher=McFarland|year=2015|isbn=9781476621074|page=138}} "[[The Ballad of the Green Berets]]" by [[Staff sergeant#United States|Staff sergeant]] [[Barry Sadler]] is released. It became the No. 1 hit in the U.S. for the five weeks spanning March 1966.{{cite web|url=https://www.worldradiohistory.com/Archive-All-Music/Billboard/60s/1966/Billboard%201966-12-24.pdf|title=Billboard Top records of 1966|publisher=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|date=24 December 1966|page=34|access-date=24 September 2020}} ; 1–8 January [[Operation Marauder]] was conducted by the U.S. [[173rd Airborne Brigade Combat Team|173rd Airborne Brigade]] and the [[1st Battalion, Royal Australian Regiment]] (1 RAR) in the [[Đồng Tháp Mười|Plain of Reeds]], [[Mekong Delta]]. The operation resulted in 114 VC and three U.S. killed.{{cite book|last=Tolson|first=John|title=Vietnam Studies: Airmobility 1961–1971|publisher=Department of the Army|date=1973|isbn=9781494721848}}{{PD-notice}}{{rp|86}} ; 3 January The PAVN bombarded a [[Special Forces (United States)|Special Forces]] [[Civilian Irregular Defense Group]] camp at [[Khe Sanh Combat Base]] near the [[Vietnamese Demilitarized Zone]] (DMZ) with 120mm mortars, the heaviest weapon they had used in the war. Defending the combat base were American and South Vietnamese Special Forces, [[Nung people|Nung]] and [[Bru people|Bru]] ([[Degar|Montagnard]]) irregulars and militia forces.Prados, John (2004), ''Valley of Death: The Siege of Khe Sanh'', Annapolis: US Naval Institute Press, pp 37-44. {{ISBN|1591146968}} In his message to the [[Tricontinental Conference 1966|Tricontinental Conference]], [[Che Guevara]] called for creating "two, three many Vietnams." to fight imperialism in the southern hemisphere.{{Cite book|last=Stanley|first=Issac|title=Dreaming Revolution: Tricontinentalism, Anti-Imperialism and Third World Rebellion|publisher=Routledge|year=2019|isbn=9781138652002|page=159}} ;6 January The [[Student Nonviolent Coordinating Committee]] (SNCC) became the first African-American civil rights organization to publicly oppose the war.{{cite book|last=Misiroglu|first=Gina|title=American Countercultures: An Encyclopedia of Nonconformists, Alternative Lifestyles, and Radical Ideas in U.S. History|publisher=Routledge|year=2015|isbn=978-0765680600|page=816}} ;7 January Commander of [[Military Assistance Command, Vietnam]] General [[William Westmoreland]] is [[Time (magazine)|''Time'']] magazine's [[Time Person of the Year|Man of the year]].{{cite web|url=https://content.time.com/time/covers/0,16641,19660107,00.html|title=General Westmoreland, Man of the Year | date=January 7, 1966|publisher=Time|access-date=20 July 2020}} A [[Claymore mine]] exploded at [[Tan Son Nhut International Airport]] gate, killing two persons and injuring 12.{{cite book|last=Pike|first=Douglas|title=The Vietcong Strategy of Terror|publisher=US Mission, Saigon|year=1970|url= https://www.vietnam.ttu.edu/reports/images.php?img=/images/231/2311404008a.pdf|pages=93–115}}{{PD-notice}} ; 8–14 January [[Operation Crimp]] was a joint US-Australian military operation in the [[Ho Bo Woods]], {{convert|20|km|mi}} north of [[Cu Chi]] in [[Binh Duong Province]], about {{convert|56|km|mi}} north-east of Saigon.{{cite book|last=Coulthard-Clark|first=Chris|title=The Encyclopaedia of Australia's Battles |edition=Second|publisher=Allen and Unwin|year=2001|isbn=1-86508-634-7}}{{rp|280}} The operation was conducted by the U.S. [[1st Infantry Division (United States)|1st Infantry Division]] and 173rd Airborne Brigade and 1 RAR resulted in 128 VC killed and 92 captured and 14 U.S. and 8 Australians killed.{{cite book|last=McNeill|first=Ian |title=To Long Tan: The Australian Army and the Vietnam War 1950–1966. The Official History of Australia's Involvement in Southeast Asian Conflicts 1948–1975. Volume Two|publisher=Allen & Unwin|year=1993|isbn=1-863732829}}{{rp|442–3}} ;9-11 January Operation Flying Tiger VI was an ARVN and ROK [[Capital Mechanized Infantry Division|Capital Division]] search and destroy operation in [[Bình Định Province]]. The operation resulted in 192 VC and 11 ARVN/ROK killed.{{cite web |url=http://www.dcbsoftware.com/ccSEA/Chronology/MACV_1966.html |title=MACV Command History Chronology - 1966 |publisher=Dcbsoftware.com |date= |accessdate=2010-07-31 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120305100137/http://www.dcbsoftware.com/ccSEA/Chronology/MACV_1966.html |archive-date=2012-03-05 |url-status=dead }} ;12 January In his [[1966 State of the Union Address|State of the Union Address]] President [[Lyndon Johnson]] told Congress and television viewers that the nation could afford both the funding of the cost of social programs and an ongoing war, saying "I believe that we can continue the [[Great Society]] while we fight in Vietnam."{{cite book|last1=Gelb|first1=Leslie|last2=Betts|first2=Richard|title=The Irony of Vietnam: The System Worked|publisher=Brookings Institution Press|year=1979|isbn=978-0815730712|page=267}} ;15 January - 25 February [[File:Photograph of Troops Moving across a Rice Field in Search of Viet Cong.jpg|thumb|right|101st Airborne soldiers advancing through field during Operation Van Buren]] [[Operation Van Buren]] was a harvest security operation conducted by the [[101st Airborne Division|1st Brigade, 101st Airborne Division]] and the South Korean [[2nd Marine Division (South Korea)|2nd Marine Brigade]] in the [[Tuy Hòa]] Valley, [[Phú Yên Province]]. The operation resulted in 346 PAVN killed and 33 captured, 55 U.S. and 45 Koreans killed.{{cite book|last=Carland|first=John|title=Combat Operations: Stemming the Tide, May 1965 to October 1966|publisher=Center of Military History United States Army|year=1999|url=https://history.army.mil/html/books/091/91-5/CMH_Pub_91-5-B.pdf|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120926060443/http://www.history.army.mil/html/books/091/91-5/CMH_Pub_91-5-B.pdf|url-status=dead|archive-date=September 26, 2012|isbn=9780160873102}}{{PD-notice}}{{rp|185–9}} ;17 January VC in Kien Tuong Province detonated a mine under a highway bus, killing 26 civilians, seven of them children. Eight persons were injured and three missing. ;25 January A USAF [[Fairchild C-123 Provider|C-123K]] lost power and crashed after take-off from [[An Khe]], en route to [[Bong Son]] killing all 46 persons on board.{{cite web|url=https://aviation-safety.net/database/record.php?id=19660125-0|title=Aircraft accident Fairchild C-123K Provider|publisher=Aviation Safety Network|date=20 August 2020}} ;26 January In a meeting with Johnson [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] senator [[John Sherman Cooper]] urged him to forgo his announced plan to resume bombing of North Vietnam and negotiate a settlement instead.{{cite journal|last=Johns|first=Andrew L.|title=Doves Among Hawks: Republican Opposition to the Vietnam War, 1964–1968|journal=Peace & Change|volume=31|issue=4 |date=October 2006|page=591|doi=10.1111/j.1468-0130.2006.00392.x}} ;28 January The U.S. [[Selective Service System]] announced that it would change its guidelines for conscription of college students and college-bound high school graduates, by barring "Class 2-S" draft deferments for students whose grades were in the lower half of their freshman class, the lower one-third of their sophomore class or the lower one-fourth of their junior class.{{cite news|title=College Draft Change Set - Students To Be Judged By Tests, Rank In Class|newspaper=Lincoln (NE) Star|date=29 January 1966|page=1}} ;28 January - 17 February [[Operation Double Eagle]] was conducted by U.S. [[1st Marine Division]] and ARVN [[2nd Division (South Vietnam)|2nd Division]] in [[Quảng Ngãi Province]]. The operation resulted in 312 VC killed and 19 captured and 24 Marines killed.{{cite book|last=Shulimson|first=Jack|title=U.S. Marines in Vietnam: An Expanding War 1966|publisher=History and Museums Division, Headquarters, U.S. Marine Corps|year=1982|url=https://www.usmcu.edu/Portals/218/US%20Marines%20in%20Vietnam%20An%20Expanding%20War%201966%20%20PCN%2019000308600.pdf|isbn=9781494285159}}{{PD-notice}}{{rp|19–34}} ;28 January - 6 March [[File:1st Cavalry Division deploys, Operation Masher, January 1966.jpg|thumb|right|1st Cavalry Division CH-47s deploy artillery during Operation Masher]] [[Operation Masher]] was a combined U.S., ARVN and [[Republic of Korea Army]] operation in Bình Định Province conducted by the U.S. [[1st Cavalry Division (United States)|1st Cavalry Division]], ARVN [[22nd Division (South Vietnam)|22nd Division]] and ROK Capital Division. The name "Operation Masher" was changed to "Operation White Wing", because Masher was deemed too crude for 'nation-building' by the [[White House]]. The operation resulted in 2,150 PAVN/VC, 288 U.S. and 10 Koreans killed.{{rp|214–5}} Masher failed to result in any decisive victories by the allies, but temporarily disrupted PAVN/VC control of the rural areas of the province. Masher and subsequent operations in Binh Dinh created large numbers of refugees who fled their homes to escape the fighting.{{cite book|last=Krepinevich|first=Andrew|title=The Army and Vietnam|publisher=Johns Hopkins University Press|year=1986|isbn=978-0801836572|pages=222–3}} ;29 January The VC killed a Catholic priest, Father Phan Khac Dau, 74, at Thanh Tri, Kien Tuong province. Five other civilians, including a church officer, were also killed. ;31 January After a 37-day moratorium that had started on 24 December 1965, the U.S. resumed [[Operation Rolling Thunder]], the bombing of North Vietnam. Among the first targets destroyed were a bridge at [[Đồng Hới]], a highway ferry complex in [[Thanh Hóa Province]] and barges near the city of [[Vinh]].{{cite news|title=U.S. Bombs N. Viet Again — Raids End Lull in Action Begun Christmas Eve|newspaper=Chicago Tribune|date=31 January 1966|page=1}} ==February== ;2 February At [[Belmore Park]] in [[Sydney]], three young Australian men became the first persons to burn their draft registration cards as a protest against Australia's participation in the war.{{cite book|last=Scalmer|first=Sean|title=Dissent Events: Protest, the Media and the Political Gimmick in Australia|publisher=University of New South Wales Press|year=2002|isbn=978-0868406510|pages=4–5}} Special Forces [[Master Sergeant]] [[Donald W. Duncan]] appeared on the cover of ''[[Ramparts (magazine)|Ramparts]]'' under the caption "I quit". He was one of the first service members to speak out against the war.{{cite news|newspaper=The New York Times|title=Donald W. Duncan, 79, Ex-Green Beret and Early Critic of Vietnam War, Is Dead|author=Robert McFadden|date=6 May 2015|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2016/05/07/us/donald-w-duncan-79-ex-green-beret-and-early-critic-of-vietnam-war-is-dead.html}} A VC squad ambushed a jeep of South Vietnamese information workers, killing six and wounding one in [[Hậu Nghĩa Province]]. ;4 February Senator [[J. William Fulbright]], chairman of the [[United States Senate Committee on Foreign Relations|Senate Committee on Foreign Relations]] began a series of hearings on the war. Johnson took Fulbright's criticism of the war as a personal betrayal by his former friend.{{cite book|last=Karnow|first=Stanley|title=Vietnam: A History|publisher=Viking Press|year=1983|isbn=9780670746040}}{{rp|486}} ;6 February to 6 March Operation Thừa Thiên 177 was an ARVN [[1st Division (South Vietnam)|1st Division]] operation in [[Thừa Thiên Province]]. The operation resulted in 183 PAVN/VC and 17 ARVN killed. ;7 February [[File:Honolulu Conference on the Vietnam War - A1916-26a.jpg|thumb|right|Honolulu Conference]] In an apparent attempt to upstage the Fulbright Hearings, Johnson and Premier [[Nguyễn Cao Kỳ]] of South Vietnam convened with other officials at [[Camp H. M. Smith]] in [[Honolulu, Hawaii]] to discuss the course of the war.{{cite web|url=https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1964-68v04/ch2|title=Foreign Relations of the United States, 1964–1968, Volume IV, Vietnam, 1966 January 31–March 8: The Honolulu Conference; Congressional Hearings on the War|publisher=Office of the Historian United States Department of State}} Television was broadcast in South Vietnam for the first time, as the [[United States Navy]] used [[Stratovision]] sending a [[Lockheed C-121 Constellation|C-121 Constellation]] to carry transmitting equipment, videotape machines and a small television studio aloft. The C-121 took off from [[Tan Son Nhut Air Base]], climbed to {{convert|10,500|ft}}, then flew in a slow oval pattern at {{convert|170|mph}} and, at 19:30, transmitted the first [[Vietnam Television (1966–75)|THVN]] programs to outdoor television sets that had been tuned to Channel 9.{{cite book|last=Hinds|first=Lynn|title=Broadcasting the Local News: The Early Years of Pittsburgh's KDKA-TV|publisher=Penn State Press|year=2010|isbn=978-0271014388|page=33}} ;7 February - May 1972 The USAF begins [[Operation Shed Light]] to develop night and adverse weather strike capabilities to interdict PAVN/VC operations. ;10 February The [[People's Republic of China]] (PRC) accused the [[Soviet Union]] of forcing North Vietnam into peace negotiations with the U.S.{{rp|155}} ;13 February A USAF [[Ryan Model 147#Ryan Model 147E|Firebee 147E]] unmanned aircraft with electronic intelligence monitors was sent on a one-way mission to be shot down by the [[S-75 Dvina|SA-2 antiaircraft radar and missile defense system]] being used by North Vietnam. The drone was picked up by the radar and destroyed, but not before "finally acquiring the long-mysterious command uplink and downlink signals" that were used in the SA-2 operation and relaying the data back to a nearby [[Lockheed DC-130|DC-130]] aircraft; acquisition of the signal led to developing methods to jam it as well.{{cite book|last=Zaloga|first=Steven|title=Red SAM: The SA-2 Guideline Anti-Aircraft Missile|publisher=Osprey Publishing|year=2011|isbn=978-1846030628|page=18}} Operation An Dan 14/66 was an ARVN operation in [[Long An Province]]. the operation resulted in 150 VC and 21 ARVN killed. ;14 February Two mines exploded beneath a bus and a three-wheeled taxi on a road near Tuy Hòa, killing 48 farm laborers and injuring seven others. ;15-21 February Operation Thang Long 234 was an ARVN operation in [[Darlac Province]]. The operation resulted in 270 VC and 62 ARVN killed. ;16-19 February In the [[Battles of Nakhang#First battle of Nakhang|First Battle of Nakhang]] the PAVN attacked the [[Royal Lao Army]] (RLA) garrison at [[Lima Site 36]] in Na Khang. The attack was successful but U.S. air support inflicted heavy losses on the PAVN.{{rp|152}} ;17 February The "Three-point Proposal" for ending the war was presented at the [[United Nations]] headquarters in New York by a spokesman for Secretary-General [[U Thant]], calling for cessation of bombing of North Vietnam by the United States, a scaling down of military activities and an agreement by all sides to enter into discussions with representatives of the VC.M. S. Rajan and T. Israel, "The United Nations and the Conflict in Vietnam", in ''The Vietnam War and International Law'', Volume 4: The Concluding Phase (Princeton University Press, 2015) p124 ;18 February The PRC consulate in [[Phong Saly]], [[Laos]], was heavily strafed by gunfire and the [[Beijing]] government charged that four American fighter jets had attacked "with more than 600 bullets", as well as dropping eight bombs to the east of the city, {{convert|20|mi}} from the border with China.{{cite news|title=China Charges Attack by U.S.|newspaper=Chicago Tribune|date=20 February 1966|page=1}} Second Lieutenant [[Carol Ann Drazba]] and Second Lieutenant Elizabeth Ann Jones were among seven killed in a helicopter crash northeast of Tan Son Nhut Air Base. They were the first of eight women in the U.S. military killed in Vietnam.{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/45309717/two_army_nurses_killed_in_vietnam/|title=Two Army Nurses Killed in Vietnam Copter Crash|date=1966-02-20|work=Dayton Daily News|access-date=2020-02-21|pages=1}} ;19 February U.S. Senator [[Robert F. Kennedy]] became the first member of the Senate to break with President Johnson in proposing that the VC be allowed "a share of power and responsibility" in peace talks with the United States.{{cite book|last=Greenwald|first=Richard|title=Exploring America's Past: A Reader in Social, Political, and Cultural History, 1865-present|publisher=University Press of America|year=1996|page=242}} ;19 February to 1 March Operation Double Eagle II was conducted by the BLT [[2nd Battalion, 3rd Marines]], [[2nd Battalion, 9th Marines]] and [[2nd Battalion, 7th Marines]] in the [[Quế Sơn District|Quế Sơn Valley]]. The operation resulted in 125 VC killed and ten captured for the loss of 6 Marines killed.{{rp|34–5}} ;21-5 February [[Operation Mastiff]] was conducted by the U.S. 1st Infantry Division in [[Dầu Tiếng District]] against the PAVN [[9th Division (Vietnam)|9th Division]]. The operation resulted in 61 PAVN and 17 U.S. killed.{{rp|175}} ;22 February to 2 March Operation Lam Son 235 was a search and destroy operation conducted by two regiments of the ARVN 1st Division in [[Quảng Trị Province]]. The operation resulted in 444 PAVN/VC and 35 ARVN killed.{{rp|248}} ;23-4 February The [[Battle of Suoi Bong Trang]] was fought on the night of 23–24 February 1966 between the U.S. 1st Brigade, 1st Infantry Division and Australian 1 RAR and PAVN/VC. The battle occurred during Operation Rolling Stone, a major American security operation to protect engineers building a tactically important road in the vicinity of Tan Binh, in central Binh Duong Province, {{convert|30|km|mi}} northwest of [[Bien Hoa Air Base]]. The battle resulted 154 PAVN/VC killed and 15 captured and 11 U.S. killed.{{rp|180–1}} ;23 February - 29 March The 1st Marine Division deployed to South Vietnam, establishing its headquarters at [[Chu Lai Base Area]].{{rp|9,128}} ;25 February to 24 March [[Operation Garfield]] was conducted by the 3rd Brigade, 25th Infantry Division in Darlac Province. The operation resulted in 122 PAVN/VC and 21 U.S. killed. ;26 February - 3 March [[Operation New York]] was a sweep operation conducted by the U.S. [[3rd Marine Division]] northwest and east of [[Phu Bai Combat Base]]. The operation resulted in 120 VC killed and seven captured and 17 Marines killed.{{rp|52}} ;26 February - 25 March [[File:NARA 111-CCV-361-CC33838 101st Airborne soldiers climbing hill Operation Harrison 1966.jpg|thumb|right|101st Airborne soldiers during Operation Harrison]] [[Operation Harrison]] was conducted by the 1st Brigade, 101st Airborne Division in Phú Yên Province. The operation resulted in 288 PAVN killed and 35 captured and 43 U.S. killed and two missing.{{rp|193}} ==March== ;3-8 March [[Operation Cocoa Beach]] was conducted by the U.S. 3rd Brigade, 1st Infantry Division along [[National Route 13 (Vietnam)|Highway 13]] near [[Lai Khê Base Camp|Lai Khê]]. The operation resulted in 199 VC and 15 U.S. killed.{{rp|178}} ;4-7 March [[File:Company F 2.7 Marines Operation Utah.jpg|thumb|right|Company F, 2/7th Marines during Operation Utah]] [[Operation Utah]] was conducted by the 1st Marine Division and three battalions of the ARVN [[Republic of Vietnam Airborne Division|Airborne Division]] northwest of [[Quảng Ngãi province|Quảng Ngãi]]. The operation resulted in 600 PAVN killed and five captured and 98 Marines and 30 ARVN killed.{{rp|119}} ;7 March [[HMM-164]] arrived in South Vietnam making the first combat deployment of the [[Boeing Vertol CH-46 Sea Knight|CH-46A Sea Knight]].{{cite book|last=Daugherty|first=Leo|title=The Vietnam War Day by Day|publisher=Chartwell Books, Inc.|year=2002|isbn=978-0785828570}}{{rp|77}} ;7-23 March [[Operation Silver City]] was conducted by the 1st Brigade, 1st Infantry Division and the 173rd Airborne Brigade in [[Biên Hòa Province]]. The operation resulted in 353 PAVN/VC and 11 U.S. killed.{{rp|183}} ; 9–10 March The [[Battle of A Shau]] was waged between the PAVN and U.S. and ARVN. The battle began on March 9 and lasted until March 10 with the fall of the special forces camp of the same name. The battle resulted in an estimated 800 PAVN killed, five U.S. missing and 196-288 ARVN killed or missing.{{cite web|url=https://archive.org/stream/projectcheco-a487011/a487011_djvu.txt|title=The Fall of A Shau|publisher=Project CHECO, Headquarters PACAF|date=18 April 1966}} ; 10 March South Vietnamese Premier Kỳ relieved General [[Nguyen Chanh Thi]] as ARVN commander in [[I Corps (South Vietnam)|I Corps]] in the northern city of [[Huế]]. Thi was accused of "siding with the Buddhists" in their long-standing dispute with the South Vietnamese government.{{cite web |url=http://www.thehistorynet.com/vn/blbuddhist/index1.html |title=The 1966 Buddhist Crisis in South Vietnam |publisher=Historynet |date=April 2005 |author=Brush, Peter |accessdate=2010-07-16 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110717003857/http://www.thehistorynet.com/vn/blbuddhist/index1.html |archive-date=2011-07-17 }} Thi was relieved after several days of demonstrations by Buddhists led by [[Thich Tri Quang]] and Thich Tam Chau. The Buddhists protested against economic conditions, corruption, and American influence and demanded that President [[Nguyễn Văn Thiệu]] and Kỳ resign. The [[Buddhist Uprising]] was called the Struggle Movement. U.S. Ambassador in [[Saigon]], [[Henry Cabot Lodge Jr.]] did not object to Thi's dismissal.{{rp|128–30}} ;15 March [[I Field Force, Vietnam]] was activated with its headquarters at [[Nha Trang]]. [[II Field Force, Vietnam]] was activated with its headquarters at [[Long Binh Post]]{{cite book|last=Eckhardt|first=George|title=Vietnam Studies: Command and Control|publisher=Department of the Army|location=Washington, D.C.|url=http://www.history.army.mil/books/Vietnam/Comm-Control/index.htm|date=1991|oclc=1030922|access-date=2021-08-27|archive-date=2017-10-19|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171019184830/https://history.army.mil/books/Vietnam/Comm-Control/index.htm|url-status=dead}}{{PD-notice}}{{rp|53–4}} ;18 March [[File:Tuy Hoa- Fifteen civilians were killed in the explosion of a homemade Viet Cong mine on a country road HD-SN-99-02085.jpg|thumb|right|Victims of the 18 March mine explosion]] A VC mine explosion killed 15 civilians on a country road 8 km west of Tuy Hòa. ;19-23 March [[Operation Oregon]] was conducted by the 1st Marine Division on the [[Street Without Joy]] approximately 36 km northwest of Huế. The operation resulted in 48 VC killed and eight captured and 11 Marines killed.{{rp|69}} ;20-4 March Operation Cuu Long 15 was an ARVN operation in [[Kien Tuong Province]]. The operation resulted in 219 VC and three ARVN killed. ;20-5 March [[Operation Texas (Vietnam)|Operation Texas]] was a 1st Marine Division and ARVN 2nd Division and Airborne Division operation northwest of Quảng Ngai. The operation resulted in 283 PAVN/VC and 99 U.S. killed.{{rp|127}} ;20-8 March Operation Kings was a 1st Marine Division operation 25 km southwest of Da Nang. The operation resulted in 58 VC and six U.S. killed.{{rp|78–97}} ;21 March Operation Lê Lợi 15 was an ARVN Special Forces operation in Darlac Province. the operation resulted in 134 VC and 10 ARVN killed. ;23-7 March Operation Maeng Ho V was an ROK Capital Division search and destroy operation in Bình Định Province. the operation resulted in 349 VC and 17 ROK killed. ;24-6 March Operation Dan Chi 211/B was an ARVN operation in Ba Xuyen Province.
